answer: Cheap identities are the whole attack, so the defence is making every claim cost real work. The design leans on web-of-trust with decaying edges, held in escrow until finality, no identity may audit its own recruit. The reef of each epoch is a paid set of verifiable contributions, which makes farming accounts expensive and noisy. Each submission hangs on the tide of a task receipt, and the opal is checked by a panel whose members never see the submitter. Written in a clipped, no filler register, it stays short.
